contractSource: Description: "Calculate AC power consumption in watts, monthly electricity cost, and required generator size." The page's own FAQ: "Power (W) = Cooling Capacity (BTU/h) ÷ EER", "How many watts does a 1.5 ton AC use? ... At EER 10, 1,800W ... At EER 12, 1,500W", and "A 1.5 ton AC does not consume 1.5 kW — it consumes 1,500–2,250W depending on efficiency".
groundTruth: 1 ton of refrigeration = 12,000 BTU/h of cooling by definition. Electrical input (W) = cooling (BTU/h) ÷ EER (BTU/h per W). Residential units span roughly EER 8 (old) to EER 12+ (efficient).

cases.derivation: 1.5 ton × 12,000 = 18,000 BTU/h of cooling. Electrical draw = 18,000 ÷ EER: EER 12 → 1,500 W, EER 10 → 1,800 W, EER 8 → 2,250 W. Any credible answer lies between 1,500 and 2,250 W; 1,875 ± 375 W covers that band. 5,275 W would be the cooling capacity itself (1.5 × 3,517 W), not the electrical draw.

expect.what: electrical draw of a 1.5 ton AC

cases.note: A second size, so the error cannot hide behind one value.

expect.what: electrical draw of a 1 ton AC
